author: marioevz
content: cc <@830368514225340436> too since he helped refactoring many of the functions affected by this proposal

author: gurukamath
content: I think the biggest question that needs to be answered first is if we are ok breaking the invariant that gas goes down monotonically in a callframe. As mentioned in the PR, this could give awkward results for contracts that use gas diff before and after to estimate call gas usage

author: gurukamath
content: As far as the change itself, it makes sense and should not super complicated imo. Would defer to the clients on that one though

author: chfast
content: GAS is not monotonic in a frame already, e.g. GAS SSTORE GAS.

author: marioevz
content: In Osaka spec or current EIP-8037 spec?

author: gurukamath
content:
I guess one can also argue that the `before_gas; CALL; after_gas; diff` pattern is already kind of broken. 

It returns inconsistent results depending on if the reservoir was used at all i.e. it returns child frame’ `state_gas + execution gas` if no reservoir was used for state operations and `execution_gas` if only the reservoir was used for state operations (and all possible results in between)

author: chfast
content: In the current 8037 spec. In Osaka it always goes down (storage refunds are only collected during execution, applied in the end of a tx)

author: chfast
content: Yes, but this will like break real 4337 bundles: the diff will wrap and strange things will happen. Do we have any 8037→4337 impact analysis?

author: marioevz
content: Even if we do this, I don't think it solves the GAS-no-longer-monotonic issue as the culprit is state refunds happening in-line, isn't it?

author: chfast
content: yes, you are right in principle
